newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia foresees lack of pilots in coming years.
newsitem.headline: Russia foresees lack of pilots in coming years.

text.p: Russia will suffer a shortage of pilots and other flight specialists in three or four years because so many are leaving the field or retiring, a senior aviation official said on Wednesday.
Yuri Karetsky, head of the pilots' department of the Federal Aviation Service (FAS), said about 5,000 pilots had retired last year and more were expected to retire in the coming years.

"Only 300 graduated pilots and flight specialists started working for Russian airlines in 1996," he said. "The prestige of working as a civil aviation pilot has fallen compared with the Soviet era, despite very high salaries for this country."
Karetsky said an experienced pilot working for the state-owned Aeroflot airline earned $1,800 a month. The average monthly wage in Russia is about $150.
On the other hand, smaller Russian airlines have tried to cut the number of pilots as a cost-saving step. "It is a very dangerous tendency," Karetsky said.
"In three or four years Russian airlines may not have middle-aged pilots," he said, adding pilots in their 40s were especially important since they were experienced but not too old.

Part of the problem of bringing up new pilots stems from the financial plight of Russia's education system. Russia has five higher flight training schools, but few students want to study there because they are concerned about the future of the profession.
"We hope to get money from the budget to improve this system," Karetsky added. --Viktor Anoshkin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
